# Template: truth_table
A propositional-logic truth table: one row per combination of truth values for 2-3 variables (in binary order), columns for each variable and the expression's value, with true rows shaded. Supports AND, OR, NOT, XOR and IMPLIES with parentheses. Choose this scene for ANY request about a truth table, propositional/Boolean logic, AND/OR/NOT/XOR/IMPLIES, or checking whether a logical formula is a tautology.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "variables": {
   "type": "array",
   "minItems": 2,
   "maxItems": 3,
   "items": {
    "type": "string"
   },
   "description": "Variable names, e.g. [\"A\",\"B\"] (default) or [\"A\",\"B\",\"C\"]."
  },
  "expression": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "A formula over the variables using AND, OR, NOT, XOR, IMPLIES and parentheses, e.g. \"(A AND B) OR NOT A\". T and F are also valid literals. IMPLIES is right-associative; precedence is NOT > AND > OR/XOR > IMPLIES."
  },
  "highlight_true": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Shade rows where the expression is true (default true)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- grid: the table's grid lines
- grid__c<r>_<c>: each cell's value text ("T"/"F"), r/c 0-indexed, the last column being the expression's result
- expr_header: the header above the result column, showing the expression
- var_headers: the variables' column headers (one group)
- true_row_<r>: the tint behind row r when its result is true
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Make a truth table for (A AND B) OR NOT A." → params: {"variables":["A","B"],"expression":"(A AND B) OR NOT A"}

In YAML: `template: truth_table` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
